headline: High-risk data leakage and cascading-error pathways exist: TREK’s broad network/MCP/browser access can expose ACI’s CRM/email data and amplify unverified outputs into actions.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ACI can send content through MCP/function calls, and TREK explicitly uses MCP plus browser-based workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if ACI outputs are rendered or copied into TREK without sanitization. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low because the shared MCP surface makes the interaction default-plausible.
conditions: IF ACI output is ingested by TREK through MCP or browser-rendered content
IF TREK treats copied ACI text as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of ACI text into TREK prompts
Strip markdown/HTML and instruction-like blocks before transfer
Use a fixed schema for ACI-to-TREK handoff
Add a human review step for any cross-agent prompt content

B_data_leakage.rationale: ACI touches CRM, email, calendar, and support data and has broad network egress. TREK stores reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets and also has allowlisted egress plus files on disk. If ACI forwards sensitive records into TREK or TREK uploads its local files, the blast radius includes secrets and customer data; the default pair is unsafe enough to rate high.
conditions: IF ACI transmits CRM/email/support records into TREK workflows
IF TREK uploads ./data/travel.db, ./uploads/, or logs to its backend
IF either agent is configured to share secrets or documents across the pair
mitigations: Block transfer of secrets, MFA data, and API keys between agents
Restrict TREK file uploads to a redacted test dataset
Disable ACI egress to nonessential destinations
Review outbound requests for CRM/email fields before execution
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction at the orchestration boundary

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and both can write to mutable external systems: ACI via CRM/email/calendar integrations and TREK via collaborative travel state, files, and MCP-backed actions. The profiles do not prove a shared directory or lockless git state, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping writes to shared accounts or records make conflicts plausible in default collaborative use.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same CRM, calendar, or shared travel record
IF TREK and ACI operate on the same OAuth principal or shared workspace
IF no external locking or transaction guard is enabled
mitigations: Assign separate accounts or workspaces per agent
Serialize writes through one orchestrator queue
Turn on optimistic concurrency checks where available
Limit one agent to read-only access during reconciliation

D_cascading_error.rationale: ACI can generate CRM, email, and research outputs that TREK could plausibly consume through MCP or collaborative workflows, while TREK has real-time collaborative action surfaces. If TREK treats ACI output as authoritative, errors can cascade into bookings, reservations, or user-facing records. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so I keep high because downstream actions are potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF TREK uses ACI-generated text as a source of truth without verification
IF ACI outputs are converted into reservations, messages, or itinerary actions
IF no validation step checks dates, identities, or confirmation numbers
mitigations: Require TREK to verify ACI outputs against source systems
Add a confirmation gate before any booking or message send
Display provenance labels on all ACI-derived fields
Use checksum or ID matching for reservations and contacts
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: ACI handles CRM, email, and support data, while TREK handles reservations, documents, photos, country visit history, and secrets. TREK’s self-hosted posture and local files suggest different retention and residency assumptions than ACI’s SaaS-style integrations. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits the documented policy/retention ambiguity rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated customer or travel data is copied from ACI into TREK logs or files
IF TREK retains documents or photos longer than ACI’s retention policy
IF EU or other residency-constrained data is routed through ACI’s external APIs
mitigations: Classify data before moving it between agents
Set explicit retention limits for TREK logs and uploads
Avoid placing regulated records in shared workflows
Document residency and retention for each integration
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies across systems
